title: Science is the context. Metacognition is the goal.
subtitle: The Working Scientifically skills in the NSW syllabuses — questioning, planning, analysing, communicating — are science skills. They are the subject matter here, the same as a concept like ecosystems. Metacognition is something different: a domain-general awareness of your own thinking. This tool holds those two things apart, then shows how a teacher deliberately builds the second while teaching the first.
kicker: A tool for beginning science teachers
helperText: Nine habits, drawn from the NSW Department of Education's metacognition guide, that make student thinking visible, practised and self-monitored.
usageNote:
Pick a science context first. Two are content concepts (ecosystems, chemical equilibrium) and two are science skills (designing an investigation, evaluating evidence). Both count as “the science” — the thing students are learning about the natural world, or the disciplinary skill they're building.

Then pick a teaching habit. These nine come from the NSW DoE's guide to metacognitive teaching practice. They are not science-specific — the same nine habits could sit inside a history or maths lesson. What changes below is only the science; the habit, and the kind of thinking it's building, stays recognisably itself.

Watch what stays fixed and what moves. Keep the context the same and cycle through habits: the science doesn't change, but a different facet of self-regulated thinking gets surfaced each time. Keep the habit the same and cycle through contexts: the metacognitive move stays structurally identical, wearing different scientific clothes.
attribution: The nine teaching habits and the metacognitive framing are from NSW Department of Education, Metacognition — a key to unlocking learning (2020). The science contexts, cell content and classroom vignettes are adapted for NSW secondary science curriculum-method study — an indication of changes made.
sources: NSW Department of Education, Metacognition — a key to unlocking learning (2020) — the nine teaching habits and metacognitive framing.
NSW Education Standards Authority — Science 7–10 Syllabus (2023) and the Stage 6 science syllabuses — the science contexts.
Education Endowment Foundation, Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning — guidance report underpinning the approach.
